chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Art Tatum arrives at the Rhythm Club with Fats Waller
summary: The blind Art Tatum came to the Rhythm Club with Adelaide Hall's group and Fats Waller gathered the pianists; Jackson had earlier heard him in Toledo.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: And there was a lot of good music came out of the rhythm club. But one of the most memorable days that I'll never forget at the rhythm club is when to me one of the greatest piano players that ever lived came through there. He come through New York --
Wait a minute. I'll get to that.
He came to New York with Adelaide Hall.

She was going to take him to Europe to play for her. He came in the rhythm club and sat down and was blind. And Fats was there at the time and Fats heard him and he went and got every piano kind of player that he thought he could find. He went and got the Lion. He got Jimmy -- James P. Johnson, all the piano players that he could find to come and hear. This was a phenomenon to him. It was Art Tatum.
And from then on Fats, he just took Art by the arm and just led Art anywhere he wanted to go. That was his man.
And Art never forgot him, you know. And if you listen to Art Tatum's solos, a lot of times there always will be a measure in there of Fats Waller somewhere.
Yes, yeah. He'll throw a little stride in there for you.
: (Unintelligible.) He could really do that, too, can't he?

Oh, he could do anything. Anything. I first heard him in Toledo, Ohio, when I was with McKinney's band and nobody knew about him. He was playing in Charlie's Chicken Shack in Toledo, Ohio, and he used to come around to McKinney's band to listen and Don would usually have him sit in.

Art Tatum, yes. And when he came to New York, I knew him. You know, the bunch of guys who was in Don's band, like Inge and Buddy Lee and myself, and Langston Curl and the guys in Don's band who was from Detroit knew him, you see. And that's one thing about Rhythm Club. That's a happening that I'll never forget as long as I live.
